newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Everbright may be on way to blue chip status.
newsitem.headline: China Everbright may be on way to blue chip status.

text.p: China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd has failed to impress investors for the past five years but its move into Hongkong Telecommunications Ltd may set the stage for elevation to blue chip status, analysts said.

The China-backed holding company baffled investors last week when it agreed to buy CITIC Pacific Ltd's 7.74 percent stake in Hongkong Telecom, possibly signalling a shift in focus to telecoms from finance.
"I think it is going to become the next Chinese blue chip in Hong Kong," said one fund manager.

The Hong Kong-based, Beijing-controlled company has been trading and investing in Hong Kong since 1983, almost as long as China International Trust and Investment Hong Kong (Holdings) Ltd, the parent company of CITIC Pacific Ltd.
Both conglomerates are directly under the control of China's State Council or cabinet.

But while CITIC Pacific has already reached blue chip status, China Everbright Holdings' three listed subsidiaries in Hong Kong - China Everbright Technology Ltd, China Everbright International Ltd, and China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd - have failed to produce solid financial results, analysts said.
One banker close to the Everbright group said the decision to sell the Telecom stake from one conglomerate to another must have been taken at State Council level.

"It is possible that we are seeing a division of labour or objectives (between CITIC Pacific and China Everbright) in Hong Kong, with China Everbright now set to concentrate on telecommunications," he said.
The appointment of Zhu Xiaohua last year as chairman of Everbright Holdings was welcomed by investors because of his solid banking and finance background.

He was head of the Bank of Communications in Shanghai before serving as the deputy head of the People's Bank of China for two years in Beijing, said Li Hui, head of China research at Indosuez W.I. Carr.
Zhu left the central bank to head the China Everbright Group Ltd, a financial services conglomerate based in Beijing.
Despite the purchase of the Hongkong Telecom stake, analysts are still divided as to the group's future direction.
Some analysts said they expected to see China Everbright develop its banking and finance operations.
"The emphasis has clearly been on China Everbright IHD," said an analyst with a U.S. brokerage. "We don't know why they have made such a big investment in telecommunications at this stage."

China Everbright-IHD Pacific's assets are primarily in banking and insurance. It has a five percent stake in Hong Kong listed National Mutual Asia Ltd and a 20 percent interest in International Bank of Asia Ltd
But since the announcement of the acquisition, market focus has shifted to China Everbright Technology as the likely future recipient of the Telecom stake.
Shares of Everbright Technology rose to a high of HK$2.025 on Wednesday from HK$0.92 on May 8, just prior to the announcement of the deal.
But the acquisition elicits more questions than answers regarding the Everbright group's long-term strategy.
Everbright Technology is seen as too small to absorb the HK$11.4 billion stake in Hongkong Telecom, analysts said.
Even after the recent surge in its share price, the company had a market capitalisation of only HK$1.58 billion based on Friday's closing price of HK$1.44.

Everbright Technology has already made one major shift in its direction. Since Zhu took over, the company has disposed of most of its manufacturing operations and said it would actively explore investment in information technology.

There has also been market speculation that parent Everbright Holdings might inject its mobile phone projects into Everbright Technology. The parent is also a minor shareholder in China United Telecommunications Corp (Unicom).
